assumptions: The operating company contracts directly with asset owners for the accounts whose relationship it claims to control, while referral partners retain their separate customer relationships.
Customer contracts clearly distinguish analytical readiness work from qualified engineering approval and allocate professional and product-adjacent liability accordingly.
Customers can lawfully provide adequate site records and may grant narrowly defined rights to non-identifying derived records, but neither access nor renewal is assumed without a signed agreement.
Qualified engineers and compliant equipment suppliers are available on replaceable, nonexclusive terms.
No annual recurring revenue, workflow licensing, data moat, or favorable contribution margin is assumed until demonstrated by paid use.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid engagements from a narrowly defined owner cohort showing price and conversion; fully loaded contribution margin after referrals, founder labor, engineer review, insurance, revisions, and support; measurable reductions in decision time, rework, downtime, or total cost; paid refresh or portfolio expansion; signed reusable data rights; and a repeatable acquisition channel independent of one family relationship.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Owners of aging systems can benefit from resolving repair-versus-repowering choices before a fault becomes an emergency, especially when model, firmware, topology, certification, and site constraints make generic lookup unsafe. A vendor-neutral, auditable decision package is coherent, although the packet does not show that this is a neglected rather than routinely bundled workflow.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Downtime, diagnostics, parts obligations, and modernization are evidenced paid events, and warranty expiry or a recorded fault gives the offer a credible trigger. Willingness to prepay for an independent readiness dossier, buy a refresh, or pay again for execution remains unknown, particularly when an incumbent service provider already owns the maintenance mandate.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepayment, pass-through hardware, and a 20,000 PLN launch cap remove the predecessor's inventory and working-capital exposure. The model is still labor- and expert-review intensive, with no demonstrated price, contribution margin, acquisition cost, conversion, repeat rate, operating leverage, or owner earnings; a one-off local consultancy would not support the founder's wealth objective.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Post-warranty or unsupported commercial PV fleets with meaningful downtime exposure form a reasonably focused initial segment. Its reachable size remains unquantified after filtering for unresolved need, budget ownership, poor OEM alternatives, site criticality, and readiness to share adequate records.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Direct owner contracts and vendor neutrality could win trust in conflicts or multi-vendor fleets, but OEMs, installers, engineering firms, and O&M providers can bundle diagnosis, compatibility review, procurement, and repowering. The owned workflow does not yet confer a difficult-to-match segment position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven workflow could expand from individual sites to portfolios, additional inverter families, adjacent components, new regions, and eventually software or workflow licensing. That path depends on enough reusable structure and outcome data emerging from heterogeneous site-specific engineering work.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Company-owned software, normalized schemas, direct contracts, and permitted outcome records offer the beginnings of a compounding asset. The workflow is initially copyable, customers may withhold durable data rights, the records may remain sparse or non-comparable, and no evidence shows that they improve decisions or retention.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A portable, vendor-neutral evidence pack with competitive execution options can reduce uncertainty and avoid premature hardware commitment. No measured reduction in decision time, rework, downtime, or total cost establishes a behavior-changing advantage over direct OEM, installer, engineer, or O&M service.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Aging PV fleets, warranty and support expiry, planned repowering, and evolving Polish certification requirements increase the number and complexity of lifecycle decisions. These forces favor readiness work, although rapid OEM replacement pathways limit the opportunity to unsupported or otherwise poorly served cases.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The founder has a lawful pilot-introduction route through the family installer, and direct owner contracting plus nonexclusive installer/O&M referrals could become repeatable. There is no signed channel access, conversion evidence, acquisition-cost evidence, or proof that intermediaries will refer instead of bundling the work themselves.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The capital-light analytical workflow aligns with the founder's data skills, AI leverage, and five-hour daily limit, while qualified engineering and field work can be contracted. Execution still requires clean customer records, careful professional-liability boundaries, current regulatory interpretation, data-rights contracting, and dependable nonexclusive expert capacity.

highest_value_structural_change: Embed the dossier as a recurring portfolio lifecycle and compliance workflow for one narrowly defined asset-owner or O&M cohort, with contractual refresh triggers, outcome-data rights, measurable service levels, and software-supported reuse while keeping engineering approval and hardware supply independent.
main_structural_strength: A customer-prepaid, inventory-free workflow turns a real technical decision into bounded analytical work, keeps capital exposure low, allows qualified experts to retain approval responsibility, and lets the founder own the software and permitted derived records.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed control point is an easily copied service workflow whose recurring demand, margins, data advantage, and route from local project work to a defensible high-value business are all still structurally uncertain.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: SolarEdge and SMA already provide rapid replacement or engineered repowering pathways, and ordinary OEM, installer, engineering, and O&M relationships can bundle the same diagnosis and procurement work; the packet contains no paid evidence that owners value a separate independent dossier enough to unbundle it.
